title: Well, that didn't last long ...
text:
Well, that didn't last long .... UPDATE Sep 26, 2015:

In week 5 of use, and not "heavy" use at that, the guide on one side split making it impossible to use. This showed such promise initially and I really thought I had a winner, but it failed in a fairly spectacular way. The design is good, but the quality of the materials (the bamboo) isn't. I'm going back to my plastic slicing guide, ordering a new one (the old one lasted almost 5 yrs).

Live and learn, I guess ...

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I absolutely love this. I've been using a plastic one that just wasn't very sturdy and the upright guides had a nasty habit of snapping off at the slightest provocation. I wanted to replace it and decided on this after looking at a number of options and reading reviews.

I make all my own bread using a bread machine and mixes I purchase from an online source. My machine is a no-frills basic unit but has been super reliable over the past 7 yrs ([[ASIN:B00067REBU Sunbeam 5891 2-Pound Programmable Breadmaker, White]] and makes a 1.5- to 2.0-lb loaf. So I opted for the "larger" version of this slicer.

I love that there are 3 sizes from which to choose. I usually use the smallest size when I'm making sandwiches (especially grilled cheese!), and the others when I'm just enjoying a slice of bread with dinner. I use an extra-long bread knife, too [[ASIN:B00091SCV4 Chicago Cutlery Walnut Tradition 10-Inch Serrated Bread/Slicing Knife]] with a 10-in blade and it works just fine with this. Yes, the loaf sticks up over the top of the guides but it's not that difficult to line things up to get a perfect slice.

I've had it a few weeks and I've gone through 4 loaves of bread with it so far with no issues at all. With the guide "plate" in place, it's sturdy and doesn't move or flex. Seriously, if you follow the instructions that come with it and make sure you flip the sides all the way around to the "back," then insert the plate, everything stays in place nicely.

Overall, I'm really impressed with it so far. If I notice any durability issues with further use, I'll update this review accordingly. But for now, this is exactly what I needed and it's working out just fine.

features: 3 Groove sizes allows you to slice 3 Different slices - 1.2cm, 1.0cm, 0.8cm
Designed to fold easily for compact storage
Made form 100% bamboo Wood, Natural, environmental friendly and pollution free
Great for bakery and homemade bread, even loaf cakes
Dimensions: 12" x 7 ½ x 6 ½ (high) Folded: 12" x 7 ½ x 1 ½ (high)
description: Are you tired of your homemade bread not being sliced evenly? Of having odd pieces of bread leftover for the trash? We've got the solution for you and it’s quite simple! Slicing bread with this DB-Tech bread slicer has never been easier; just place the bread in the slicer and cut you knife along the grooves to create a perfect slice every time. This slicer can slice 3 different thicknesses, an average store bought slice of bread is 1cm thick; this slicer allows you to cut your bread in 0.8cm, 1cm and 1.2cm slice giving you the ultimate variety, and if you enjoy really thick slices you can slice your bread in every other slot to produce an even thicker slice. The slicer is made from 100% bamboo wood and is extremely durable. Its spring loaded flip out design makes it easy to quickly open and fold it away in 2-3 seconds for easy storage

The Difference between the 2 Bread Cutters are the width, The wide is 7 ½ Inch and the narrow is 6 ½.
